SMTO-SKL-0161 — SMTO isn't sure which GitHub repository you mean

GUID: 4cc641da-46a2-53e7-abda-45f940a5e998
Slug: github-repository-ambiguous
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • Your folder or saved references point to more than one GitHub repository, such as your copy and the original, or SMTO couldn't read the full list. SMTO won't guess, so nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Repeat your request and name the repository as owner/name, copied from its address on github.com. A named repository takes priority over the folder's links, so SMTO no longer has to choose.
  2. Or type @ in the message box and choose a single saved Git Repository entry from Parameter Store. One saved repository gives SMTO one clear target.

What success looks like

  • SMTO answers about the repository you named and shows its owner and name.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't remove links from your project folder just to make this go away.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Repository resolution found more than one distinct github.com repository among the bound references or Git remotes, or the captured Git working context reports an incomplete remote list.

What this means

  • Repository references produce multiple distinct remotes, or captured Git Repository metadata says its remote list is incomplete. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Repository references produce multiple distinct remotes, or captured Git Repository metadata says its remote list is incomplete.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect explicit owner/repo and complete fork/upstream remote evidence.

How to fix it

  • resolve() saw multiple distinct github.com remotes (fork plus upstream counts) or a verified git working context with remotes_complete=false; neither origin nor the first remote is preferred. Pass the exact host and owner/repo, or refresh the Git Working Context so its remote list is complete.
  • Supply the exact intended host and owner/repo, or refresh complete repository-reference evidence before selection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • One intended exact repository is chosen without origin or first-remote guessing.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
